Work from the project root, the main folder of the course. Read each step before you run its R chunk. All data are simulated. These exercises cannot show a finding about a real disease.

The [glossary](../docs/glossary.md) explains the course words. Each module reads its input files from disk. You do not need a saved R workspace.

```{r knit_setup, include=FALSE}
start_dir <- setwd(if (file.exists("config.R")) "." else "..")
if (requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = getwd())
setwd(start_dir)
```

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("R/guided.R")
cfg <- guided_init()
```

## Module 2 at a glance {#module-2-overview}

**What you will do.** You will check the files that the laboratory sent. You will convert them to the format of [PLINK 2](../docs/glossary.md#plink-2), the free program used throughout this course. Then you will correct [strand](../docs/glossary.md#strand) differences, add disease and age information, and save a first [checkpoint](../docs/glossary.md#checkpoint).

**What you will learn.**

- What the [genotype](../docs/glossary.md#genotype) files contain and why they must stay together.
- How to measure [missingness](../docs/glossary.md#missingness), the share of genotypes that could not be read.
- Why some variants cannot be oriented to a strand.
- What a [genome build](../docs/glossary.md#genome-build) is and why GRCh37 and GRCh38 must not be mixed.
- How to join disease and age to the right person.

**How long it takes.** About 60 minutes. Steps 2.5 and 2.6 take the longest, because they introduce new ideas.

## 2.1 The starting files {#step-2-1}


<!-- step_meta: {"success_line": "You see 2,016 sample wells and 299,523 variant entries before QC."} -->
### What we do

We identify the complete set of files exported by the laboratory. We keep these input files unchanged.

### Why

The laboratory supplied a matched [BED/BIM/FAM](../docs/glossary.md#bed-bim-fam) trio. BED holds the calls, BIM the variants and FAM the samples. Review [the format map at 1.9](module_01_from_dna_to_array_data.Rmd#step-1-9) and [the fields at 1.10](module_01_from_dna_to_array_data.Rmd#step-1-10) if needed. Keep the companions in their original order. Equal counts alone do not prove that identities match.

These are starting files with deliberate quality problems, not a cleaned cohort. Later steps find the poor samples and variants.

### You need

You need module 0 completed and the export inspection from module 1.

### Command

```{r s2-1}
print(check_bed(cfg$input))
head(read_fam(cfg$input))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: this step needs no PLINK command. The R code above is the complete command.

R reads the files and shows the values. It does not change the genotype files.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

You see 2,016 sample wells and 299,523 variant entries before QC. Each well has its own [FID/IID](../docs/glossary.md#fid-iid) pair, the two identifiers that name a sample in the files.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message. Check that the previous step finished. Keep the command and the console output (the text printed in R). Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Why must the FAM file stay together with the BED and BIM files?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

The FAM file gives the sample identities and their order. PLINK needs this information to decode the genotype matrix.

</details>

### Files created

None.

## 2.2 Convert to PLINK 2 native format {#step-2-2}


<!-- step_meta: {"success_line": "The 2,016 samples and 299,523 variants are all kept."} -->
### What we do

We convert the matched BED, BIM and FAM files to PGEN, PVAR and PSAM files.

### Why

PGEN stores the genotypes. PVAR describes the variants (the sites). PSAM describes the samples. These three files are the [native format](../docs/glossary.md#pgen-pvar-psam) of PLINK 2. The BED, BIM and FAM files stay useful for older programs. Neither format records the genome build. The conversion must keep the same samples and variants in the same order.

### You need

You need the original matched files that you checked at 2.1.

### Command

```{r s2-2}
out <- guided_path(cfg, "2.2")
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", cfg$input, "--make-pgen", "--out", out), paste0(out, c(".pgen", ".pvar", ".psam")))
stopifnot(all(guided_counts(out) == c(2016, 299523)))
guided_source_checkpoint(cfg)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --bfile data/course/lab_export/sim2026_lab --make-pgen --out results/guided/s2-2_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--bfile` takes the shared file-name prefix of the BED, BIM and FAM files. `--make-pgen` writes a new set of native files. `--out` sets the prefix (the first part) of the output file names. `--threads 2` limits PLINK to two worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the memory budget to 2048 MiB (about 2 GB). The R helper prints the exact command with your own safe paths.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

The 2,016 samples and 299,523 variants are all kept. PLINK can mark the [reference allele](../docs/glossary.md#reference-allele) (REF) as provisional. This happens because a BED file does not say which allele matches the genome reference.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message. Check that the previous step finished. Keep the command and the console output (the text printed in R). Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Does converting BED to PGEN automatically convert GRCh37 coordinates to GRCh38?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. The storage format and the genome assembly are two separate properties.

</details>

### Files created

`s2-2_state.pgen/.pvar/.psam`, and the command and console logs in the output folder.

## 2.3 Sample and variant tables {#step-2-3}


<!-- step_meta: {"success_line": "The PSAM file has 2,016 rows and the PVAR file has 299,523 rows."} -->
### What we do

We read the sample table and the variant table. We do not change them.

### Why

FID and IID are text identifiers, not row numbers. Keep any leading zeros, such as in 007. Always join tables by these identifiers.

The variant table (PVAR) has columns for the chromosome, the position, the site ID and the alleles. An [rs identifier](../docs/glossary.md#rs-identifier) can be shared by several resources, even when each resource uses a different genome assembly (a full reference sequence of the genome) for the coordinates. An Illumina name may name an array assay (one test on the chip) and not a unique place in the genome.

### You need

You need the native files from 2.2.

### Command

```{r s2-3}
samples <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "2.2"), ".psam"))
variants <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "2.2"), ".pvar"))
head(samples)
head(variants)
check_ids(samples, "Laboratory samples")
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: this step needs no PLINK command. The R code above is the complete command.

R reads the files and shows the values. It does not change the genotype files.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

The PSAM file has 2,016 rows and the PVAR file has 299,523 rows. Different assay IDs do not prove that every site is unique. Two assays can still test the same place in the genome.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message. Check that the previous step finished. Keep the command and the console output (the text printed in R). Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Should you join two tables by row number when they have the same length?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. Match the FID/IID pair or the site identifier. Then check that every required record found its match.

</details>

None.

## 2.4 First overview {#step-2-4}


<!-- step_meta: {"success_line": "You get a sample report and a variant report."} -->
### What we do

We measure how much data is missing, before we decide which samples or sites to remove.

### Why

The [call rate](../docs/glossary.md#call-rate) is the fraction of genotypes that were observed. Missingness is one minus the call rate. A missing genotype is also called a no-call.

A sample report asks whether a well has many no-calls. A variant report asks whether a site fails in many wells. We look at both, because they point to different problems.

### You need

You need the native files from 2.2.

### Command

```{r s2-4}
out <- guided_path(cfg, "2.4", "missing")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "2.2"), "--missing", "--out", out))
smiss <- guided_table(paste0(out, ".smiss"))
vmiss <- guided_table(paste0(out, ".vmiss"))
summary(as.numeric(smiss$F_MISS))
summary(as.numeric(vmiss$F_MISS))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-2_state --missing --out results/guided/s2-4_missing --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--pfile` reads a set of native files by their shared prefix. `--missing` writes one report for samples and one for variants, and it removes nothing. `--out` sets the prefix of the output file names. `--threads 2` limits PLINK to two worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the memory budget to 2048 MiB. The R helper prints the exact command with your own safe paths.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

You get a sample report and a variant report. Some values are much worse than the main group. No samples and no variants are removed at this step.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message. Check that the previous step finished. Keep the command and the console output (the text printed in R). Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### What this check can reveal

It can reveal a well that performed badly, probes (the DNA pieces on the chip that detect a variant) that failed, or groups of affected samples. A threshold is a rule for deciding. It does not tell you the cause of the problem.

### Quick check

If F_MISS is 0.03, what is the call rate?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

0.97, or 97%.

</details>

### Files created

`s2-4_missing.smiss`, `.vmiss` and the logs.

## 2.5 Alleles and strand {#step-2-5}


<!-- step_meta: {"success_line": "400 sites are flipped and 3,013 sites are excluded. 2,016 samples and 296,510 variants remain."} -->
### What we do

We compare the allele pairs from the laboratory with the supplied plus-strand annotation. We flip the pairs that are complementary. We remove the sites that are ambiguous or incompatible.

### Why

An [allele](../docs/glossary.md#allele) is one of the versions of a variant, written as a base: A, C, G or T. DNA has two strands, and the bases pair up in a fixed way: A with T, and C with G. An A/C site on one strand reads T/G on the other strand.

Some sites are [palindromic](../docs/glossary.md#palindromic-snp): A/T and C/G. After a strand flip, they show the same pair as before. So the pair alone cannot tell us the orientation. This course removes these sites instead of guessing from allele frequency.

Allele order is not strand. A/G and G/A contain the same pair.

### You need

You need the BIM file from 2.1, the annotation from 1.1 and the PGEN files from 2.2.

### Command

```{r s2-5}
bim <- read_ws(paste0(cfg$input, ".bim"), header = FALSE)
ann <- guided_table(file.path(cfg$data_dir, "array", "sim2026_array_annotation.tsv"))
k <- match(bim[[2]], ann$Name)
stopifnot(!anyNA(k))
pair <- function(a, b) ifelse(a < b, paste0(a, b), paste0(b, a))
observed <- pair(bim[[5]], bim[[6]])
reference <- pair(ann$Ref_Plus[k], ann$Alt_Plus[k])
complement <- chartr("ACGT", "TGCA", reference)
complement <- pair(substr(complement, 1, 1), substr(complement, 2, 2))
palindromic <- reference %in% c("AT", "CG")
flip <- !palindromic & observed != reference & observed == complement
exclude <- palindromic | (observed != reference & observed != complement)
flip_file <- guided_list(bim[[2]][flip], guided_path(cfg, "2.5", "flip.txt"))
exclude_file <- guided_list(bim[[2]][exclude], guided_path(cfg, "2.5", "exclude.txt"))
stopifnot(sum(flip) == 400L, sum(exclude) == 3013L)
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "2.2"), "--flip", flip_file, "--exclude", exclude_file,
  "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "2.5")))
stopifnot(all(guided_counts(guided_path(cfg, "2.5")) == c(2016, 296510)))
ops <- data.frame(option = c("--flip", "--exclude"), value = c(flip_file, exclude_file))
guided_register(cfg, "2.5", "2.2", 2016, 296510, operations = ops)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-2_state --flip results/guided/s2-5_flip.txt --exclude results/guided/s2-5_exclude.txt --make-pgen --out results/guided/s2-5_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--flip` replaces each base by its complement at the listed IDs. It does not swap the effect allele. `--exclude` removes the listed IDs; `--make-pgen` saves the corrected copy. `--out` sets the prefix of the output file names. `--threads 2` limits PLINK to two worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the memory budget to 2048 MiB. The R helper prints the exact command with your own safe paths.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

400 sites are flipped and 3,013 sites are excluded. 2,016 samples and 296,510 variants remain. The planted problem categories overlap, so do not simply add their nominal counts.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message. Check that the previous step finished. Keep the command and the console output (the text printed in R). Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### What this check can reveal

It can reveal strand differences, palindromic sites and incompatible alleles. Agreement with this annotation does not prove that the genome reference sequence itself is correct.

### Quick check

Can A/T versus T/A tell you whether the strand is correct?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. The pair is palindromic, so the strand cannot be found from the pair alone.

</details>

### Files created

The flip and exclusion lists, and `s2-5_state.pgen/.pvar/.psam`.

## 2.6 Genome builds and lift-over {#step-2-6}


<!-- step_meta: {"success_line": "The exercise has 10,000 sites. 9,970 of them map to the same chromosome, and eight of these map to the reverse strand in this chain file."} -->
### What we do

We convert the separate GRCh37 exercise to GRCh38 in R. We use a chain file for this one direction. We keep the exercise apart from the main analysis.

### Why

GRCh37 and GRCh38 are two different reference assemblies of the human genome. A coordinate is a chromosome and a position in one named assembly. Changing the build label or the rsID does not change the coordinates.

A [lift-over](../docs/glossary.md#lift-over) converts coordinates from one assembly to the other. It uses a [chain file](../docs/glossary.md#chain-file), which records which intervals of the two genomes are aligned. After a lift-over, a site can be unmapped (it has no match), it can move to another chromosome, or it can map to the reverse strand.

UCSC intervals are zero-based and half-open, which means they start counting at 0 and exclude the end point. The course positions are one-based, which means they start counting at 1. Review the unmapped sites and the reverse-strand sites. Do not accept a conversion that nobody documented.

### You need

You need the small GRCh37 exercise supplied at 0.5. You also need the official hg19-to-hg38 chain file. It is part of the course data, in the folder `data/course/grch37_exercise/`. You do not need to download it. The main array is already GRCh38, so we do not lift it again.

### Command

```{r s2-6}
legacy <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "grch37_exercise", "legacy_grch37")
bim37 <- read_ws(paste0(legacy, ".bim"), header = FALSE)
chain <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "grch37_exercise", "hg19ToHg38.over.chain.gz")
require_files(chain)
lifted <- guided_liftover(paste0("chr", bim37[[1]]), bim37[[4]], chain)
keep <- !is.na(lifted$position) & lifted$chromosome == paste0("chr", bim37[[1]])
map <- data.frame(ID = bim37[[2]][keep], POS = lifted$position[keep])
map_file <- guided_path(cfg, "2.6", "update_map.tsv")
write.table(map, map_file, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
keep_file <- guided_list(map$ID, guided_path(cfg, "2.6", "mapped.txt"))
args <- c("--bfile", legacy, "--extract", keep_file, "--update-map", map_file)
reverse <- bim37[[2]][keep & lifted$strand == "-"]
if (length(reverse)) args <- c(args, "--flip", guided_list(reverse, guided_path(cfg, "2.6", "reverse.txt")))
run_plink(cfg, c(args, "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "2.6", "grch38")))
ann <- guided_table(file.path(cfg$data_dir, "array", "sim2026_array_annotation.tsv"))
k <- match(map$ID, ann$Name)
stopifnot(all(map$POS[!is.na(k)] == as.numeric(ann$Position_GRCh38[k[!is.na(k)]])))
print(c(input_sites = nrow(bim37), mapped_same_chromosome = sum(keep), reverse_strand = length(reverse)))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --bfile data/course/grch37_exercise/legacy_grch37 --extract results/guided/s2-6_mapped.txt --update-map results/guided/s2-6_update_map.tsv --make-pgen --out results/guided/s2-6_grch38 --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--extract` keeps only the IDs that were mapped successfully; `--update-map` reads the ID and the new position from two columns. If R finds reverse-strand mappings, add `--flip` with the reverse list that R generates. The exercise keeps only the sites that stay on the same chromosome, and it reports the sites it excludes. `--out` sets the prefix of the output file names. `--threads 2` limits PLINK to two worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the memory budget to 2048 MiB. The R helper prints the exact command with your own safe paths.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

The exercise has 10,000 sites. 9,970 of them map to the same chromosome, and eight of these map to the reverse strand in this chain file. PLINK prints a warning that the base-pair positions are now unsorted. This warning is expected: the new GRCh38 positions are not in the old order. The resulting exercise variants are not sorted by position. Sort them explicitly before any operation that needs sorted input. Mapped positions whose identifier also appears in the course annotation agree with GRCh38. The main 296,510-site state from 2.5 is unchanged. A lift-over can lose sites, so record the mapping counts that are reported.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message. Check that the previous step finished. Keep the command and the console output (the text printed in R). Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### What this check can reveal

It can reveal build mismatches, gaps and reverse mappings. A chain file does not check alleles and does not impute genotypes.

### Quick check

Does a successful position lift-over guarantee that REF and ALT now match the destination reference?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. You must still check the alleles and the reverse-strand mappings.

</details>

### Files created

`s2-6_update_map.tsv`, the mapped and reverse lists, and the separate `s2-6_grch38` files.

## 2.7 Add phenotype and covariates {#step-2-7}


<!-- step_meta: {"success_line": "All 2,016 wells are matched, and 296,510 variants remain."} -->
### What we do

We join the extra information to each well by its identity. A well that holds a labelled technical replicate gets the information of the original person.

### Why

The [phenotype](../docs/glossary.md#phenotype) is the outcome that we study. Here the variable Disease is 1 for controls and 2 for cases. A case is a person with the disease and a control is a person without it.

Age is a [covariate](../docs/glossary.md#covariate). A covariate is a measured variable that the model uses to account for other influences.

Recorded sex is supplied for the sex check. We never guess it from the row order.

A [technical replicate](../docs/glossary.md#technical-replicate) is the same person measured in a second well. It inherits the information of the original person. It stays a separate well until the duplicate review.

### You need

You need the corrected files from 2.5, and the sample sheet and phenotype table from 0.5.

### Command

```{r s2-7}
metadata <- guided_metadata(cfg)
pheno <- metadata[c("FID", "IID", "SEX", "Age", "Disease")]
names(pheno)[1] <- "#FID"
pheno_file <- guided_path(cfg, "2.7", "phenotypes.tsv")
guided_write(pheno, pheno_file)
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "2.5"), "--update-sex", pheno_file,
  "--pheno", pheno_file, "--pheno-name", "Disease", "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "2.7")))
stopifnot(all(guided_counts(guided_path(cfg, "2.7")) == c(2016, 296510)))
ops <- data.frame(option = c("--update-sex", "--pheno", "--pheno-name"), value = c(pheno_file, pheno_file, "Disease"))
guided_register(cfg, "2.7", "2.5", 2016, 296510, operations = ops)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-5_state --update-sex results/guided/s2-7_phenotypes.tsv --pheno results/guided/s2-7_phenotypes.tsv --pheno-name Disease --make-pgen --out results/guided/s2-7_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--update-sex` loads the recorded sex of each sample by its ID; `--pheno` selects the phenotype table; `--pheno-name Disease` names the yes-or-no outcome to use. `--make-pgen` stores the joined phenotype in the PSAM file. `--out` sets the prefix of the output file names. `--threads 2` limits PLINK to two worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the memory budget to 2048 MiB. The R helper prints the exact command with your own safe paths.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

All 2,016 wells are matched, and 296,510 variants remain. There are 2,000 people before we remove low-quality wells, relatives and ancestry outliers.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message. Check that the previous step finished. Keep the command and the console output (the text printed in R). Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Why must you join labelled replicate wells to their original person before you assign the phenotype?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

The phenotype describes the person. The rows of the export describe measured wells.

</details>

### Files created

`s2-7_phenotypes.tsv` and the native `s2-7_state` files.

## 2.8 Module 2 checkpoint {#step-2-8}


<!-- step_meta: {"success_line": "You get a full 2.8 checkpoint with 2,016 samples and 296,510 variants."} -->
### What we do

We save the first complete set of native files that you can restart from. We record its checked size.

### Why

The end of a module is a stable point to return to. A checkpoint is a saved copy of the analysis at one moment. Later filters can be replayed from this full copy, so we do not need to distribute every large file. A checkpoint is not evidence that anyone replicated the result.

### You need

You need the joined files from 2.7.

### Command

```{r s2-8}
guided_snapshot(cfg, "2.8", guided_path(cfg, "2.7"), 2016, 296510)
check_step("2.8", data_dir = cfg$out, work_dir = cfg$out)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: this step needs no PLINK command. The R code above is the complete command.

R reads the files and shows the values. It does not change the genotype files.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

You get a full 2.8 checkpoint with 2,016 samples and 296,510 variants. The working state matches the counts and the [SHA-256](../docs/glossary.md#sha-256) checks of its checkpoint. A SHA-256 check compares a short fingerprint of a file, to prove that the file has not changed.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message. Check that the previous step finished. Keep the command and the console output (the text printed in R). Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Which boundary should you use before you replay the early sample QC filters?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

Use the completed module 2 checkpoint at 2.8.

</details>

### Files created

`s2-8_state.*`, `checkpoints/2.8/state.*`, `checkpoints/index.tsv` and `step_counts.tsv`.

## Module 2 recap {#module-2-recap}
